claims.statement: FilesystemMiddleware is the agent-facing owner of the built-in filesystem tool set, resolves a configured backend at request or tool-call time, filters tools by resolved capabilities, and adapts backend instances or factories to the V2 protocol.

Filesystem tool input accepts `path` as a fallback alias for `file_path`, normalizes read pagination bounds, and treats malformed permission-checked paths as recoverable error ToolMessages rather than sending them to the backend.

Permission rules require absolute glob paths without `..` or `~`; rules support `**`, `*`, and brace expansion, are evaluated in declaration order with first-match-wins semantics, and allow access when no rule matches.

Read operations use `read` permissions and write-like operations use `write` permissions; `ls`, `glob`, and `grep` additionally post-filter returned entries or matches, while denied ordinary operations do not invoke their backend method.

Delete permission enforcement treats deletion as a recursive write: confirmed plain files use first-match rule ordering, but possible or ambiguous subtrees are blocked by any overlapping deny-write pattern so an allowed parent cannot remove a denied descendant.

`read_file` defaults to a 0-indexed offset of 0 and a 100-line limit; text reads expose optional line-window metadata and the middleware formats a status header above an unmodified source body, while binary reads ignore line pagination.

The middleware limits binary `read_file` payloads to 10 MiB and returns supported binary MIME types as multimodal image, audio, video, or file blocks; oversized binary reads return an error content block.

Text read output has a separate character budget estimated at four characters per token: truncation prefers complete source-line boundaries and rebuilds pagination metadata, but an oversized single line may be clipped mid-line without a misleading resume offset.

Grep is literal rather than regular-expression search, uses ripgrep fixed-string mode with a substring fallback for local files, supports output modes and file globs, and applies a total match cap whose truncation is explicitly reported.

FilesystemBackend provides local filesystem operations with optional virtual-root containment, symlink-resistant file I/O, recursive deletion, sorted non-recursive listings, and glob/search behavior that avoids following symlinked directories.

State-backed operations communicate graph-owned file changes through state updates or Pregel sends, whereas externally persisted backends return `filesUpdate: null`; the middleware converts non-null updates into LangGraph `Command` updates.

CompositeBackend routes by the longest matching path prefix, restores routed paths in listings and search results, fans out parent deletes across mounted routes sequentially, and delegates `execute` only to its default sandbox backend.

Eligible large ToolMessages are offloaded at the configured threshold, default 20,000 tokens, to `/large_tool_results/<sanitized-call-id>.txt` with a head-and-tail preview and paginated readback guidance; filesystem search/read tools are excluded from this eviction path, while `execute` is not.

A separate human-message eviction threshold, default 50,000 tokens, saves oversized latest human text under `/conversation_history/<random-id>`, tags it with `lc_evicted_to`, and replaces it at model-call time with a preview while preserving non-text media blocks.

Path-based permissions are rejected alongside unrestricted command execution because shell commands can access arbitrary paths; construction fails unless `execute` is disabled or every permission path is scoped to a CompositeBackend route, with a deferred equivalent check for backend factories.

Filesystem operation failures are normally returned as structured or formatted tool results, while invalid permission configuration, an allowlist without `read_file`, and unsafe permission-plus-execution combinations fail fast during setup.
